title: Younger musicians: J.J. Johnson, Max Roach, Miles Davis, Wardell Gray
summary: The band ended around 1946, and he kept picking up young players with something new, including Johnson, Roach and Davis.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: By that time, had your work with the studios increased?
Yes, it seemed as though it was increasing.
And you could look forward, then, to maybe having at least to think -- maybe you could have some kind of a career in Hollywood in a studio?
Yes. Although following that time, I still went out with bands from time to time. I'd get a band together and go do a series of dates, you know.
Right.
And I hadn't given up the band completely, but just as an every night affair, I had.

Right. Now in these groups that you led in '43, '44 -- this was a time I think, when you began to pick up a number of younger musicians. For a long time, you know, in your bands, you would have people you could always count on -- came in and out. But now a new generation was arising during, and just after World War II, and you began to pick up some musicians who were much younger. Among them, I think -- well, you tell me.
Well, you probably have in mind J.J. Johnson and Max Ranch Rose -- people like that.
Right.
And Freddie Webster. Actually, J.J. Johnson joined the band in 1942, in September, when we were
on the way to California, we picked up J.J. Johnson in Indianapolis.
Right.
And Max Roach was with the band, it seems, since about '44, I guess. Yeah. Freddie Webster about '44, and ...

I think I know your answer to this, but I'm gonna ask it anyway -- did you feel that these guys were playing something new that you wanted to have part of your band, or were you again, just picking up good musicians, playing good music or whatever it was?

Well, I felt that, certainly they had something new, different, fresh, young. And something I liked -- and I did want to have them with the band, and as a matter of fact, I had Miles Davis in the band in '46.
Yeah. A little bit later -- maybe in one of these pickup bands that you would put together for a few dates, rather than keep them indefinitely, you also had Wardell Gray.
Oh, yes, well, when I had Wardess Gray in 1951, with the sextette.
Right.
Had a sextette, and we played in California -- in Hollywood, actually, and then of course I had him with the band later in 1955, when we were in Las
Vegas when he came to his untimely end.
